Oman began to export oil in 1967, after Petroleum Development Oman found fields in the interior at Yibal and Fahud in the early 1960s.

The search had driven the sultan to take over the interior in the Jebel Akhdar War. Oman's oil came late and in smaller amounts than its neighbours', but it changed the country: three years later Qaboos took power and spent the revenue on roads, schools and hospitals.

The company is owned mostly by the state, with Shell as the main foreign partner. Oman has since tried to move into gas, ports, tourism and fishing, as its oil runs lower than in Saudi Arabia or the UAE.
sum: Oman began to export oil in 1967, after Petroleum Development Oman found fields in the interior at Yibal and Fahud in the early 1960s.
